result.summary: Adds `btck_witness_stack_get_items` to the C libbitcoinkernel API along with a `WitnessStackApi::GetItems` C++ wrapper method. The function performs a single O(n) traversal of a serialized witness stack, populating caller-provided arrays with pointers to each item's data and its byte size. This allows callers to inspect or copy all items in any order without repeatedly scanning the serialized stack.
result.problem: Under the serialized witness stack format introduced in #36895, item lookup requires parsing the serialization from the beginning, making random access O(n) in item index. Consumers attempting to retrieve all elements of a witness stack via `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` suffer O(n^2) runtime.
evidence: PR description: "Reading a whole witness stack with btck_witness_stack_get_item_at is O(n^2) because each call walks the items before the one it returns. This function gets every item in one O(n) pass and the caller can read them in any order."
result.scope_notes: All but the final commit belong to base PR #36895, which converts CScriptWitness to store witness stacks in serialized byte format; review for this PR is confined to the kernel API additions in commit 0b833469c1.
result.changed_since_previous: No structural change to the proposed API; the branch has been rebased on updated commits from #36895.
result.card: Adds btck_witness_stack_get_items and a C++ wrapper method WitnessStackApi::GetItems to libbitcoinkernel. Under the compact serialized witness stack representation in base PR 36895, indexing into a stack takes linear time, causing full-stack reads via btck_witness_stack_get_item_at to take O(n^2) time. This API parses the entire stack in one O(n) pass, returning pointers and sizes into caller-allocated arrays so items can be read in any order. Depends on #36895.

risk.why: Touches only libbitcoinkernel query APIs by returning pointers into existing witness stack memory, posing no consensus or validation risk.
